glm_bug_semantics: WEBrick's chunked-body reader ends with `read_header(socket)  # trailer + CRLF` (lib/webrick/httprequest.rb, read_chunked), which unconditionally re-invokes the same header parser used for the initial request head: `@header = HTTPUtils::parse_header(@raw_header.join)` overwrites the canonical request-header hash with the trailer block, then `@header.delete("transfer-encoding")` erases the only record that the request was Transfer-Encoding: chunked. A client can therefore smuggle `Content-Length: N` as a chunked TRAILER: the initial head says `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (so the CL-vs-TE conflict check in read_body never fires because read_body's self['content-length'] test runs before the trailer reparse), the trailer's Content-Length is parsed straight into @header as canonical request state, and transfer-encoding is then deleted — leaving a request whose canonical state claims both a Content-Length body framing that the server never consumed and no TE marker. Downstream, @remaining_size is reset to 0 while @header['content-length'] survives, so any component that later trusts self['content-length'] (e.g. meta["CONTENT_LENGTH"] in CGI/ERB env setup, or keep-alive pipelining logic) interprets the unread socket bytes as the next request — classic CL-via-trailer request smuggling (CWE-444). The advisory scope is 'through v1.9.2', i.e. every tagged release.
